title: PRIVACY, ACCESS CONTROL & DATA GOVERNANCE - FULL AUDIT
method: Static implementation inspection of all services + schema review + masked secret scan + live dependency vulnerability scan (pip-audit). Services were not running, so no live HTTP probes were performed; server-side auth enforcement was verified by reading every route handler.

matrix.test: Every sensitive API/model/admin endpoint requires authentication
matrix.evidence: All 15 /internal/* endpoints across risk (7), privacy (7), identity (1) require X-Internal-Token verified via hmac.compare_digest (verify_internal_token). All /admin/* (front) require server-side _require_admin JWT session. Identity /admin/* require require_role('admin'). Audit/verification compliance endpoints gated.
matrix.fix: none

matrix.evidence: /demo/seed requires authenticated fraud_id + PS14_MODE gate; /run-tests /run-security-scan /security/run-auto-scan /monitor/run-tests all call _require_admin_session inside the handler (server-side); /monitor/record requires internal token (hmac.compare_digest).
matrix.fix: none

matrix.evidence: No live secret values in code or artifacts (masked regex scan of src/scripts/reports/models/db/docs). .env values differ from documented dev defaults (SHA-256 compared, not printed). BUT dev-default literal strings 'ps14-dev-internal-token-change-me' etc. are hardcoded in scripts/live_walkthrough.sh, scripts/live_curl_walkthrough.sh, scripts/real_cases.py and documented in .freebuff/security_audit.md.
matrix.fix: Remove the token constant from scripts/real_cases.py (read INTERNAL_TOKEN from env only); scrub the 'change-me' literals from walkthrough scripts (fallback should fail, not silently use a documented token).

matrix.evidence: identity_service: hierarchical PERMISSION_MAP (user < analyst < admin), require_role/require_permission FastAPI deps; self-registration hardcodes role='user' (role not accepted from clients). All protected handlers use Depends - no UI-only checks found.
matrix.fix: none

matrix.test: Normal user cannot reach admin/model/audit functions
matrix.evidence: Front admin = separate passphrase session (scrypt hash + encrypted essentials + TOTP); audit/compliance = internal token or per-analyst passphrase; analyst endpoints require role analyst/admin; model/db access = admin-only /admin/db-query (audit-logged).
matrix.fix: none

matrix.evidence: audit_service require_compliance_token still accepts a legacy shared token fallback ('legacy-shared-token') alongside per-analyst credentials; verification_service compliance gate uses only the shared compliance_token (no per-analyst store).
matrix.fix: Remove legacy shared-token fallback once analysts.json onboarding exists; verify only per-analyst passphrases.

matrix.evidence: Regex scan (Supabase keys, postgres URLs w/ creds, AWS keys, JWTs in JSON, private keys, generic long secrets) over src/scripts/reports/models/db/docs/.freebuff: only dev-default 'change-me' strings and an unused dev TLS key (certs/ps14.key) found; .env, db/, certs/ are gitignored.
matrix.fix: Delete unused certs/ps14.key + ps14.crt (no code references them).

matrix.test: Secrets come from a secure env mechanism
matrix.evidence: Settings defaults are empty -> random per-process token_hex(32); all services call load_dotenv_and_patch and start_stack.ps1 loads .env; PS14_MODE=production (default) fails startup (sys.exit) if JWT_SECRET/PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY/INTERNAL_TOKEN/COMPLIANCE_TOKEN/EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY/CORS are not set from env.
matrix.fix: none

matrix.test: No secrets printed to logs or audit reports
matrix.evidence: Source grep of logger/print calls found no token/password/secret emission; audit payloads reviewed at all 9 append_audit_event call sites - pseudonymous (fraud_id, event_id, scores, decision, outcome, ids); db/test_runner_debug.log clean.
matrix.fix: none

matrix.test: At-rest protection of stored PII (DB-1 identity)
matrix.evidence: users table: phone_encrypted/email_encrypted/address_encrypted are Fernet-encrypted LargeBinary, but full_name (Text), account_number, account_type and kyc_doc_ref are PLAINTEXT despite the code comment claiming 'PII is column-encrypted'. db/identity.db sits in a plain SQLite file.
matrix.fix: Encrypt full_name and account_number at rest (same Fernet path as email/phone); keep only the fields the UI strictly needs plaintext, or move DB behind OS-level disk encryption. Do NOT alter jwt_secret/pii_encryption_key derivation (breaks existing DB-1 decryption per AGENTS.md).

matrix.test: DB-2 / DB-3 / DB-4 contain no raw PII or card data
matrix.evidence: features.db: derived features only, device_hash keyed+truncated, location_id/recipient_id opaque tokens (loc-3, recip-0 in demo), no raw amounts (amount_ratio/bucket only). risk.db: fraud_id/event_id/scores/reason_codes. audit.db: pseudonymous payloads (hashed txn refs).
matrix.fix: Note: if real deployments send real recipient/location identifiers, DB-2 stores them raw by design (see AGENTS.md) - hash them or classify as sensitive.

matrix.test: Logging does not over-collect sensitive fields
matrix.evidence: No app-level PII logging found; but uvicorn default access logs record full request paths, and several endpoints take fraud_id (and /alerts event ids) in query strings.
matrix.fix: Disable or redact uvicorn access logs in production (or move ids into headers/body).

matrix.test: Public endpoints do not expose operational data
matrix.evidence: front_service (port 8000, public): /batch, /real-cases, /fraud-report, /monitor/metrics, /monitor/unified, /test-results, /monitor/test-results, /security/scan-history and /security/scan-latest are ANONYMOUS. They serve scenario reports containing transaction amounts (synthetic), aggregates and security-scan results. /security-scan (singular) requires admin - inconsistent with /security/scan-latest.
matrix.fix: Gate /security/scan-history, /security/scan-latest, /monitor/metrics, /monitor/unified behind the admin session; decide access policy for the demo scenario endpoints; at minimum remove inconsistency with /security-scan.

matrix.evidence: SQLAlchemy ORM throughout; privacy audit_search uses sql_text with bound :params; no f-string SQL concatenation found in service code. /admin/db-query executes raw SQL by design but is admin-session-gated and audit-logged.
matrix.fix: none

matrix.evidence: SQLite: per-store file isolation (no shared credentials). PostgreSQL mode: single shared DATABASE_URL; per-service schema enforced only when SERVICE_NAME/DB_SCHEMA are set (production gate enforces this under Docker). No per-service DB roles.
matrix.fix: In real deployment create per-service Postgres roles with least privilege; keep per-service schemas.

matrix.evidence: Dev stack is loopback HTTP (uvicorn binds 127.0.0.1); no in-process TLS. TLS termination is expected at a proxy/ingress which is not part of this repo - not verifiable here.
matrix.fix: Terminate TLS at the ingress; keep services loopback-only or mTLS between services.

matrix.evidence: Audit export is HMAC-SHA256 signed (export_signing_key) with independent verifier; but db/*.db.bak are unencrypted copies of the SQLite stores (DB-1 backup would contain plaintext full_name/account_number).
matrix.fix: Encrypt DB backups; re-verify after the DB-1 at-rest fix.

matrix.evidence: 142 packages inventoried. pip-audit (2.10.1, advisory DB reachable - 2026 entries returned) found 4 known vulnerabilities in setuptools 78.1.0 (PYSEC-2025-49, PYSEC-2026-3447, fixes 78.1.1 / 83.0.0). COMPLETENESS: torch==2.13.0+cpu could NOT be audited (local build tag absent from PyPI) - 1 of 142 packages skipped. Scanner did not fail silently: skips are reported.
matrix.fix: Upgrade setuptools to >=83.0.0. For torch, pin a PyPI-release version or document the +cpu build's exclusion from audit.

matrix.evidence: No retention policy, purge job, or deletion path for identity/features/risk/audit stores. Demo state, session cleanup exists only for sessions/rate-limiter; DBs accumulate indefinitely. audit.db is append-only by design (immutable chain) and exempt from deletion, but no documented retention schedule exists for the others.
matrix.fix: Define a retention schedule per store (e.g., features/risk N months, identity per regulation), implement purge with tombstoning where the audit chain requires it, and document deletion procedure.

matrix.test: Prior automated security scan did not claim false confidence
matrix.evidence: db/security_report.json (2026-08-22) records checks_performed: 0, files_scanned: 50, summary passed: true - a zero-check scan persisted as PASS. This audit supersedes it.
matrix.fix: Do not persist zero-check scans as passed; require checks_performed > 0 before writing a PASS verdict.

overall.sensitive_data: FAIL (DB-1 plaintext PII at rest: full_name/account_number/account_type/kyc_doc_ref; public operational endpoints)
overall.database_security: PASS (single shared cred is PARTIAL for real deployment)
overall.transport_storage: NOT TESTED for TLS (loopback dev); at-rest PARTIAL
overall.rationale: No critical authentication, authorization, or live-secret-exposure failure was found - those areas are genuinely strong (server-side role/permission gates, internal tokens on all internal endpoints, env-only secrets with a production fail-closed gate, pseudonymous audit payloads). The FAIL is driven by sensitive-data-at-rest (plaintext full_name/account_number in DB-1 contradicting the code's own encryption invariant), the absence of any data-retention policy, anonymous operational endpoints on the public front service, and unpatched setuptools CVEs - none acceptable for a system 'about to handle real financial data'.
